agents.reason_blind: @MSFT365Status 06:09 UTC (after the 04:18 UTC freeze): 'completed our efforts to address the underlying issue... restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions.' Microsoft usually ends an incident with this wording, with no further 'resolved' post (precedents MO941162, July 2025), and outlets report it as fully resolved. The main risk is a strict reading of the wording.
agents.reason: Signals add nothing (no matching market). A post-freeze Microsoft statement of restored service to all remaining customers, reported as fully restored, most likely meets the 'service restored' branch. About 10% held back for a strict reading of the wording and a small relapse risk.

About 60 hours of window left; similar incidents closed in 1–2 days, but weekend monitoring is possible.

red_team.case_for_morning: The criterion is strict about wording. 'Restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions' never says 'resolved', 'remediated' or 'fully recovered', and it points to MO1550821 'for further updates', which suggests the admin-center entry may still be open in monitoring. A strict resolver could insist on the tenant-only admin-center closure or on an exact phrase, and Microsoft could post a residual or relapse notice before Monday's load.
red_team.case_further: The 06:09:51 UTC post came after the freeze at 04:18 UTC and is a final 'service restored' update ('completed our efforts to address the underlying issue'). The criterion lists 'service restored' as qualifying and @MSFT365Status as a source, and outlets quoting Microsoft (PA via Yahoo UK, Lowyat, Digital Trends) read it as resolved. The event has in effect happened, and a relapse cannot undo a declaration, so 0.98–0.99 is defensible.
red_team.why: The statement exists, came after the freeze and fits the criterion's 'service restored' branch, and the press reports it as resolved. The only risk left is how the wording is read, which justifies a few points off 0.99 but not a return towards 0.74.
red_team.factor: outcome (the declaration itself); nothing found after 06:09 UTC that reopened or relabelled MO1550821
red_team.likeliest_failure: The resolver reads 'restored service to the remaining impacted customers' as short of 'resolved', because the post points to further admin-center updates and no explicit 'resolved' wording appears publicly by 23:59 UTC on 15 Nov.

red_team.case_for_morning: Large strikes usually come after lulls, and the current one (five nights since 317 on 9 Nov) is the longest in the window; earlier gaps were 2, 1 and 5 nights, so the hazard is rising. Falling counts fit stockpiling for a mass combined strike. Ukraine's ~1,200-drone raid and the run-up to the Berlin Coalition of the Willing meeting and the Trump–Putin meeting give motives to retaliate or signal. 0.43 already discounted the 0.50 base rate.
red_team.case_further: Only 2 of the last 7 nights reached 170, the five latest all fell below it, and the series has dropped to 96, the low of the window. No reports of strategic-bomber build-up or mass-strike warnings for 14 Nov were found, and with peace diplomacy under way Russia may be holding back mass strikes, so 0.25 is arguable.
red_team.why: The lull-hazard argument is real but already reflected at 0.33 (agents 0.28–0.40). The momentum evidence is five falling nights below 170 with no sign of strike preparation, while the lull hazard prevents going much lower. Both cases roughly cancel around 0.30–0.35.
red_team.factor: slip_class none; the new count moves the outcome (whether tonight is a mass-strike night), not the timing of the report
red_team.likeliest_failure: Russia ends the lull with a mass combined strike (often 300+ drones) on the night of 14–15 Nov, in retaliation for Ukraine's raid or as leverage before the Berlin meeting.
